title: I've played Heroes of Might and Magic 3: Remake, and I still can't believe we're getting 2 HoMMs in the same year
summary: Ubisoft is going all in on fantasy tactics.
body: After lying fallow for over a decade, Heroes of Might and Magic is enjoying a bit of a renaissance. Earlier this year, Heroes of Might and Magic: Olden Era launched into early access and will hit 1.0 in 2027. And now it's going to be joined by an old friend with a new look. The series' golden child, Heroes of Might and Magic 3, is back. Again. HoMM 3 Remake is actually the third version of the third game in the series, which was remastered back in 2015. At a glance, however, you could be forgiven for assuming that it's a brand new entry, as it boasts a new art style along with a few more tweaks. But this is still absolutely HoMM 3. (Image credit: Ubisoft) I took it for a spin over a couple of hours ahead of its Gamescom reveal, playing the simple campaign prologue and the Arrogance scenario—a popular map first introduced in HoMM 3: The Shadow of Death. It's a compact, well-paced adventure that I remember being a good place to start when you wanted to delve into multiplayer (or if you just wanted a fun comp stomp). This remains true in the remake. It's a four-player deal, and each starting position is close to a second town of the same faction, rapidly expanding your ability to rec…

title: Blue Dragon has been stuck on the Xbox 360 for 20 years, but no longer: a fantastic unofficial PC port unlocks the FPS, goes 4K, and even adds mod support
summary: This Xbox 360 recompilation proves how good fan ports can be when they aren't vibe-coded.
body: When Final Fantasy creator Hironobu Sakaguchi left Square Enix in the early 2000s, he started a new studio, Mistwalker, to keep making RPGs. For the last 20 years, every single one of his games with the exception of Fantasian has been stuck on one defunct console or another, never ported or re-released. And that's a shame, because some of them are great RPGs. (Image credit: Mistwalker) Or I should say it was a shame, until now—because as of Friday, Blue Dragon will be playable on PC thanks to a fan-made port that's likely far more impressive than an official release ever would've been. re:Blue, a static recompilation of the Dragon Quest-inspired JRPG, follows in the footsteps of the unofficial Sonic Unleashed PC port that proved how effective fan-made ports can be. These projects cleverly translate the original game code to run natively on modern PCs, but don't include any of the original assets to avoid copyright issues. This technique has proven so popular that it's inspired a wave of AI vibe-coded ports that don't take the time and care to thoroughly adapt the original game to PC. But in spite of that, the good projects—like the recent Zelda: Twilight Princess port —have made i…

body: Hello from Gamescom 2026 , where yours truly has been trying out some of the latest laptops at the Nvidia booth. The machines I was shown are made by various manufacturers, but all of them have the same core internal hardware, in the form of Nvidia's RTX Spark SOC. Which means that, alongside 20 Grace CPU cores in the custom Arm-based chip, they've also got 6144 RTX Blackwell GPU cores to play with. And that means RTX 5070 -like gaming performance, at least on paper. And in practice, each was demonstrated to be capable of running modern games at high frame rates. Exactly how high was kept under wraps, unfortunately, although it was mentioned that frame generation was in use for each. So, I wasn't able to do any benchmarking of my own, or dig into the settings menus to find out exactly what sort of DLSS/FG combination I was dealing with. Still, 007 First Light , Arc Raiders , Borderlands 4 , and F1 25 were all running without a hitch, which is apparently indicative of the smooth sailing Nvidia has experienced with Microsoft's Prism translation layer . title: Micron, the trillion-dollar memory company, refused to replace a crucial drive for current market value until Reddit got mad
summary: 'Pushing back actually worked.'
body: With the memory crisis only continuing to get worse, a PC gamer's fear right now is likely their memory, storage or GPU borking, and needing to spend an inflated price to replace it. One such Redditor had an external drive die in just one year, and Crucial only offered a refund of the original price they paid, which was a lot less than similar drives go for now. That was until they brought their problems to Reddit. Over on the PCMR subreddit , user CarefulMeasurement99 shared that they bought a 4 TB Crucial drive a year ago for $200, and when it broke, Crucial offered that original price in a refund. That same drive seems to fetch up to $800 now (thanks, AI). Crucial originally set up an RMA for the drive in order to pick it up and send it back to the company. The Redditor replied to this saying, "Due to the recent global increase in SSD prices, $199.999 is unfortunately no longer enough to purchase a new 4 TB drive in the current market", and officially requested a direct replacement. This story gets a tad complicated because Micron announced the closure of the Crucial consumer business late last year, which threw its ability to actually replace the drive into question. title: OLED gaming monitors have finally gotten so good that a Counter-Strike 2 tournament is using one
summary: The Asus ROG Swift OLED PG259QWS Ace is the first OLED to make it into a CS2 Major.
body: I've been watching the ascent of OLED with a very keen eye, primarily because as a Counter-Strike 2 gamer, I know just how promising OLEDs will be for competitive gaming. And now it seems we're at the point where they've gotten good enough in specific ways to be the official panel tech of choice in an official CS2 Major tournament. Asus' new monitor, the ROG Swift OLED PG259QWS Ace , is going to be the official monitor of the 2026 PGL CS2 major . It's a glossy tandem WOLED with a response time of 0.02 ms (GTG), which is low even for OLED. More relevant here, though, is that it's a 720 Hz, 24.5-inch panel. We've seen high refresh rate OLEDs before, but most of these (A) are 27-inch or bigger, and (B) only achieve their high refresh rates when dropped to 720p. Getting up to 1080p is ideal for pro gaming, especially in CS2, where some will want to stretch a 4:3 resolution, and 24/25-inch monitors are preferred. It might seem silly to some, but I've tested some pro-level monitors and can confirm that 24/25-inch monitors can make playing CS2 a little more comfortable, allowing you to see the entire game scene without squinting in a way that pushing a 27-inch monitor further away someho…

title: We saw The Witcher 3 – Songs of the Past in action, and the full-game remaster that's coming this year too

body: In Print This is a shorter version of an exclusive Witcher 3 – Songs of the Past cover feature that will go out in the next issue of PC Gamer magazine . Keep your eyes peeled! Surprise! Songs of the Past, The Witcher 3's third expansion, isn't kicked off by some Ciri-centric weft in the space-time continuum, nor another curt and urgent letter from Yennefer. As for Triss, well, I didn't spot a single red hair of her in the hands-off demo that CD Projekt Red and Fool's Theory gave us. It's Dandelion. Geralt's lute-plucking biographer has gone missing, and who better to find him than his best pal in the whole wide world? So when Songs of the Past releases next year, he'll be back on the path in a region of The Witcher's world we've never seen before—Dandelion's family home of Letten, in the kingdom of Redania. And he's got another surprise for you, too: a full Witcher 3 remaster that aims to make the 2015 classic feel like it released in the modern era, due for release on September 29. Over a decade since The Witcher 3's last expansion, the boys are back in town. There's No Place Like Where better to get a glimpse of Dandelion's true face than his family home? title: Metro 2039 takes us back to Moscow, but it's still got some delicious bits of Exodus in there
summary: Delicious up until you realise you've wasted all your gas mask juice trying to open a closet door.
body: Isn't it always the way? You spend so long yearning to leave home, to strike out and make a go of it all by yourself, but the second you step foot out the door you start missing it. All of it. The camaraderie and the rows, the shared meals and the constant, privacy-smothering proximity, and—of course—the mutated beasts from the overland, intent on your complete and utter destruction. This is how I imagine it went for 4A Games when it came time to make Metro 2039 , the fourth mainline game in the Metro series. Artyom is gone—he took a train off into Russia's carcass in Exodus, but Moscow and its metro endure, and 4A has returned to them for 2039. In Artyom's absence, you play someone new: The Stranger, a gruff and—in contrast to the previous three Metros—chatty protagonist who's on a quest to find and kill Hunter, the former legendary Ranger hero and (it seems) current overlord of almost the entire metro. Things have gone to pot since Artyom went interrailing. The metro's many fractious stations have largely been brought under one banner, but it is a fascist banner, ruled over by Hunter with an iron fist. Someone should probably put an end to that. title: Ubisoft forgot to make sure the Steam release of Heroes of Might & Magic 3 included the actual game
summary: Oops.
body: The HD rerelease of Heroes of Might & Magic 3 from 2015 used to be the only way to get the strategy classic on Steam, leaving many players frustrated since it lacked the expansions and the random map generator. Ask fans of the series, and they'd tell you to get the original version from GOG instead. So it should be an easy win for Ubisoft that the series' current owner finally decided to put the original version, complete with its expansions Armageddon's Blade and The Shadow of Death, on Steam at last. Its current user review rating of 80% negative suggests otherwise. Fork out $10 for it and you'll find an install that's only 23.49 KB big, which gives a "dummy executable" error message when you try to launch it. Because Heroes of Might & Magic 3 on Steam does not come with Heroes of Might & Magic 3. Somebody forgot to include the actual game files with the game. I'm sure this will be fixed soon, perhaps when France wakes up, but in the meantime the complete edition on GOG is still the best version and it's currently on sale for half-price . title: The hardware crisis has hit a new low: We're now using rats for RAM
summary: Rat computer.
body: Good news from the near future: Space travel has apparently advanced enough to allow humanity to establish a hotel on the surface of the moon. Bad news: The RAMpocalypse apparently continues unabated, forcing novel experimentation with alternate forms of computer memory not rendered wholly unaffordable by AI datacenters. Namely, rat computers. This believable projection of the current miserable state of consumer hardware comes courtesy of Ontos, the next game from Amnesia developer Frictional Games. In the trailer above, a man strapped to a chair with electrodes stuck in his head is a bit freaky, though less so than another guy who's missing everything from his upper teeth down; perhaps humanity in the future is so desperate for localized processing power that we're resorting to shoving DisplayPort cables into our brains, too. The strongest big of imagery in the trailer by far, though, is a computer the size of a wall with 60 rats connected to it in sequence. Or parallel? I'm not great on my circuitry fundamentals, but I know a rat computer when I see one. I am instinctively scared of the rat computer and the unknown potential of 60 rat minds taking the place of random access asia…

title: The Witcher 3 Remastered announced: another huge free update, and all Witcher 3 owners get the existing expansions free
summary: The update isn't just graphical, and it's out in September.
body: The Witcher 3 got a "Next-Gen Update" back in 2022, and CD Projekt Red is doing it again: The developer announced at Gamescom today that The Witcher 3 Remastered is coming September 29 as a free update for all owners of the RPG. Aside from graphical updates (of which there are many), The Witcher 3 Remastered makes changes to combat, movement, Roach riding, monster behaviors, the skill tree, and the photo mode. The kicker: Alongside the update, owners of The Witcher 3 will also get its two expansions, Blood and Wine and Hearts of Stone, free if they don't already own them. For newcomers, the expansions will be bundled with The Witcher 3 Remastered. The remaster arrives well in advance of the next expansion, Songs of the Past , which releases sometime next year. "My favorite [new feature] is the visuals. That's new textures, updated rendering, advanced path tracing, foliage, you name it," said CD Projekt Red level design lead Miles Tost at Gamescom's Opening Night Live showcase. "Geralt has never looked this good, even after all those years of retirement. "And then the other thing, definitely, is combat. It's more modern, smooth and precise. We updated the camera, the targeting syst…

title: Lego is finally fulfilling its destiny by making a city builder
summary: Took you long enough.
body: In retrospect I'm not sure why it's taken Lego so long to get here: it's made Star Wars games, Batman games... heck, it even made a Fortnite game. The first Lego videogame came out way back in 1997! But at least it's finally fulfilling its destiny: The blocks that were made for building are finally being used for a city builder. Lego Skylines was announced today at Gamescom, and yeah, it looks like the perfect fit. Have a peek at the announcement below. Looks pretty darn sweet, and looks pretty darn big. But how big? "In this cozy, customizable city-builder, your choices bring a living, breathing metropolis to life. Go big or obsess over the details. No instructions. Unlimited space," says Paradox Interactive. Unlimited space? For real? That's... quite a lot of space. "Remember hospitals to keep everyone in one piece. Wheat for the donuts. Garbage collection, sewage, and all the other things that make a city click. How it all comes together is up to you. So stick your hard hat on and greenlight your weirdest ideas," Paradox says. Sounds good to me: it's got that Lego cuteness but also looks like it doesn't skimp on the complexity. Interestingly, Lego Skylines is being developed by…

title: Path of Exile 2 is finally getting swords in December, and also the rest of the game
summary: Grinding Gear Games squeezes one more class in before the action RPG leaves early access and goes free-to-play.
body: It's finally time for the one thing every Path of Exile 2 player has been waiting for: swords. A new class and weapon type is coming to the action RPG later this year—oh, and the full 1.0 release of the game. On December 11, PoE 2 will leave early access behind and go full free-to-play, just like its predecessor. While developer Grinding Gear Games has several previously announced classes to get to eventually, the 1.0 release will at least include the one many players have been waiting for. The Gamescom Opening Night Live 2026 trailer doesn't actually give the man with the sword a title, but a post on the GGG forums calls him the duelist, which lines up with the class that was teased a while ago. It's possible he's gone through a few iterations over the last few years, but he's definitely using a sword for all the new skills. Swords are a big deal in PoE 2 because weapons are class agnostic, meaning a new weapon type is like getting a big drop of new skills for everyone to play with. I'm more of a caster player, but I can't deny how good some of them look. At one point, the mysterious swordsman pulls up a cone of icicles and slams the sword down in the middle, turning the poor mon…

title: Atari is taking another shot at reviving RollerCoaster Tycoon
summary: RollerCoaster Tycoon Wonderworks is being developed by Springloaded, makers of the excellent Let's Build a Zoo.
body: Last we saw RollerCoaster Tycoon it was in pretty rickety shape. More than a decade after RollerCoaster Tycoon 3, the follow-up—RollerCoaster Tycoon World—was released to nearly universally poor reviews. Even worse, in one of the all-time dick moves in gaming industry history, Atari launched it exactly one day before rival sim Planet Coaster was due to release. Wow. That nakedly desperate move didn't help the situation: people liked Planet Coaster and didn't like RCTW, and the Tycoon series has been silent since 2016. But here we are another decade later, and Atari is bringing RollerCoaster Tycoon back yet again—though I'm already feeling more hopeful about it. RollerCoaster Tycoon Wonderworks was announced at Gamescom today, and the new entry in the series is being developed by Springloaded, who made the excellent Let's Build a Zoo and is releasing promising gamedev sim Let's Build a Dungeon later this year. That's a good sign, at least! There's no date on the books yet, and RollerCoaster Tycoon Wonderworks won't be feature complete when it launches: it's "coming soon" to early access. Here's its page on Steam .

title: 1666: Amsterdam's early access is live now but there's still plenty that needs ironing out before I'd pay $30 for it
summary: Long road ahead.
body: It's been a long development for 1666: Amsterdam and the folks over at Panache Digital Games, but after over a decade of fighting and planning, the game's finally made it to early access. Announced at Opening Night Live , we got to see 1666: Amsterdam's last trailer before its release. It revealed the main characters Noa Brooklyn (the witch) and Aaron (the man trapped in a cat's body) as they traverse through modern day and 17th century Amsterdam on a journey to hunt down, fight, and kill the demonic Originals who have grown too greedy and powerful for their own good. (Image credit: Panache Digital Games) I played through the first hour of the game—which followed straight on from the demo—a few weeks ago, and while it did show promise I wasn't entirely convinced it was ready for early access . Well, now early access is here. I got a sneak peak and well, not a whole lot has changed. I'm happy to say I've encountered far fewer bugs. There have been a couple of crashes, but there'll be some patches yet before it's in your hands. My greatest issue, though, remains the same—1666: Amsterdam has a lot of interesting ideas which are woven together poorly. Its setting and premise are excit…

title: Battle royale goes grunge: there's a new PUBG game and it's set in the '90s
summary: PUBG: Ded.net is "a new multiplayer FPS that combines shooter gameplay with roguelite progression across runs."
body: No one is safe from '90s nostalgia, not even battle royale. A new PUBG game was announced today at Gamescom, and it's gone grunge, according to publisher Krafton. Maybe more interestingly, PUBG: Ded.net is also a roguelite, with progression across runs. Take a peek at the announcement trailer below, set to Ministry's "Jesus Built My Hotrod" (though that's industrial, not grunge) and then come back for some more details. "PUBG: DED.NET is a new multiplayer FPS that combines shooter gameplay with roguelite progression across runs, giving players new ways to experiment, adapt and build their own approach in the strange and unpredictable world of 1990’s Cascadia," says publisher Krafton. Does that mean its a blend of battle royale and extraction? It sort of sounds that way: "A match lost is never a run wasted. Every drop of blood writes the next chapter—what you scavenge in the world changes you, and that changes how you fight," Krafton says. "Mix and match dozens of abilities to build your own custom approach to combat. Use car doors as riot shields, cannibalize enemies for health, play dead, or hack payphones to steal money from rivals." As you might expect, the Steam page also has …

title: Exodus is out early next year, and I think I'm finally on board with the general Mass Effect vibes of it all
summary: You'll meet Salt and the gang in April 2027.
body: Exodus is not beating the "boy, that sure looks like Mass Effect" charges, but the more I see of it, the more I mean that as a term of endearment. Archetype Entertainment shared another peek at its sci-fi RPG during this year's Opening Night Live showcase, along with its April 7, 2027 release date. The latest trailer offered a better introduction to Salt, one of Jun Aslan's otherworldly companions. I'm sensing more of that BioWare companion magic with her reveal, and assuming she's the part of the crew I'll lovingly refer to as my child, à la Grunt. Salt is an Awakened, humanity's self-aware animal neighbors with their own organized societies, hailing from an ocean planet inhabited by an intelligent race of octopuses. She's also a cutie patootie, sassy, and (seemingly) tragic. At the end of the trailer, my new octopus daughter is left sifting through what looks like dried-up ocean life. Hell no, that's not happening under my watch as Jun. Well, at least I hope it's not. While she's the star of the show, Salt isn't the only Exodus companion we see more of in the trailer. There's also new footage of Emrys, another of Jun's alien companions, but this one isn't an Awakened. Emrys is a…

title: The next game from Hoyoverse sure looks like someone put Elden Ring's clothes on Monster Hunter
summary: Who among us doesn't love to sever the Dreadnodus?
body: As the opening reveal of this year's Gamescom Opening Night Live, HoYoverse brought its first official look at Nodusfall—a change of pace for the gacha game behemoth that looks a little bit Elden Ring, a lot bit Monster Hunter, and a whole pile of proper nouns added for good measure. While I like to think it takes more to catch my attention than forcefully mashing together two things I think are neat, I'd be lying if I said I wasn't tempted by the idea. If there's one thing Monster Hunter monsters have been missing, it's FromSoft-style primordial depression. From the looks of things, there's more than enough metaphysical malaise to go around in Nodusfall. The laws of divinity have apparently frayed, plunging creation into a state of cosmic disarray. There are 10 suns now. Ideally, there's only supposed to be one of those. Not great! Luckily for those of us who like to be given an excuse to try to fight a lizard 30 times our size, all that profound devastation seems to have produced a wide selection of giant, charismatic creatures to swordfight alongside your friends. In the reveal trailer embedded above, I saw giant bears, some sort of giant pack foxes, a horned, winged manticore,…

title: I attempted to become a professional driver in a GTA 5 where every car had no friction
summary: Gotta make ends meet somehow.
body: If you remember, uh, yesterday, then you'll remember how I have recently modded GTA 5 to essentially deactivate friction on all NPC cars. Also, all NPC cars are perpetually, unstoppably in motion. Long story short: they keep accidentally flying and/or exploding. So I thought what I could do today would be to try to become a professional driver in that world. I have installed The Getaway (Driver Missions) , a mod which lets you dial a new number in your phone in order to undertake road quests . In practice, that means driving to a place, picking a guy up, then driving that guy to another place. At some point in this process you lose the cops. All well and good, but not overly dramatic. What makes it a lot more hair-raising is every other driver on Los Santos' roads no longer obeys the laws of physics. Even driverless cars are irrepressibly compelled forwards, making it damn-near impossible to actually acquire a car to undertake these missions. Fortunately, I am a lateral thinker. I simply used my car gun to summon a car directly into a wall. As the unstoppable force met the immoveable object, I was able to get in and go about my business. Sort of.
